prompt:
Our `issues.py` issue tracker (`models.py`, `errors.py`, `constants.py`, `storage.py`, `repository.py`, `cli.py`, documented in `README.md`) only lets `list` dump every issue, unsorted and unpaginated. The team wants filtering, sorting, and paging from the command line, without breaking any existing integration that already calls `list`. Please make these four changes together:

1. In `repository.py`, extend `IssueRepository.list_issues()` with `status`, `priority`, `assignee`, and `tags` filters, plus `sort_by`, `order`, `page`, and `page_size`. Filtering is AND across everything given (an issue must match every filter, and have every requested tag - not just one of them). Sorting defaults to `id` ascending when `sort_by`/`order` aren't given; `sort_by` also accepts `created_at`, `priority`, `title`, and `status`, and `order` is `asc` (default) or `desc`. Sorting by `priority` must use severity order (`low < medium < high`), not alphabetical order. Whatever the sort key and direction, ties must always be broken by `id` ascending - `order=desc` reverses the primary key only, never the tie-break. Pagination is 1-based (`page=1` is the first page); a page past the end comes back with an empty result, not an error; `total` and `pages` must describe the whole filtered-and-sorted set, the same on every page of it, never just the current page's size. Apply filtering, then sorting, then pagination, in that order.

2. In `cli.py`, add `--status`, `--priority`, `--assignee`, `--tag` (repeatable), `--sort-by`, `--order`, `--page`, and `--page-size` flags to the `list` subcommand, wired to the new `list_issues()` parameters. `--assignee ""` (an explicit empty string) should filter down to unassigned issues; simply not passing `--assignee` applies no assignee filter at all. Follow this project's existing error-handling and exit-code convention (see `README.md` and `errors.py`) for every way one of these flags can be invalid (an unrecognized status/priority/sort field/order, a tag given as an empty string, a non-numeric or out-of-range page or page-size) - they must all fail the same way the rest of the project already fails on bad input, not with a stack trace, an argparse-formatted error, or a silently-empty result for a typo'd filter.

3. `list`'s existing callers only ever run `list` or `list --json` (a flag that has never done anything - output was always JSON) and parse a plain JSON array; they must keep getting exactly that, completely unchanged, including when `--json` is passed. `list` should only switch to a richer, paginated output shape when the command line actually contains one of the flags added in step 2 - based on whether the flag is present at all, not on whether its value happens to match the default (so e.g. `list --order asc` must use the new shape too, even though `asc` is already the default order). That new shape is a JSON object `{"items": [...], "total": ..., "page": ..., "page_size": ..., "pages": ...}`, using the defaults described above for whichever of the new flags weren't given. `page` defaults to `1`; `page_size` defaults to `20` and cannot exceed `100`.

4. Update `README.md`: document the new flags, and add a short new section with these two example invocations and their exact output: `python cli.py list --status open --sort-by priority` and `python cli.py list --page 2 --page-size 1`, both run against the three sample issues already shown elsewhere in the README ("Fix login bug" high/ren/auth, "Write onboarding docs" low/docs, "Crash on logout" high/kai/auth+bug) after issue `2` has been closed.

`summary` must keep reporting every issue regardless of anything passed to `list` - it has its own counts and should not be touched. `list`, `show`, and `summary` must stay read-only (no writes to the issue file), and every issue dict `list_issues()` hands back must stay an independent copy, same as today. Keep `add`/`show`/`close`/`delete` working exactly as they do now.
